newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo plans to privatize Comgas by Oct 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo plans to privatize Comgas by Oct 1997.

text.p: Sao Paulo state government plans to privatize its natural gas distributor Comgas and offer concessions to distribute gas in the state by October 1997, said an official at the state's Energy Secretariat.
"The sale might occur in October 1997," said Ricardo Lima, an official at the secretariat who advises investors on the state's privatization plan.
The state also plans to lift the gas distribution monopoly of Comgas by selling two or three concessions to private companies, he said.
The state government will hold a public hearing on Jan 23 when it will present investors bid specifications to hire consultants to advise on the sale, he said.

Lima said consultants would define whether the state would sell all its 80 percent stake in Comgas or retain a minority stake. The remaining 20 percent of Comgas is controlled by the Sao Paulo municipal government.
He said the state government decided to privatize Comgas because the company will need investments of around $350 million by 2000 to expand gas distribution in the state.

Currently, Comgas distributes 3 million cubic meters of gas daily but it has agreed with Petrobras to increase its daily purchases by 1.5 million cubic meters of gas by 1998 and another four million daily by 1999.
